body.statement: Derive, rather than posit, a finite correction-order map \(q(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d)\), a finite family of distance resolutions, and signed weights for \(\mathfrak H_P\) whose separate propensity and control-regression vanishing moments leave bias at most \((h_n^*/(k_n^*)^{1/d})^{\alpha+\beta}\) and whose Hoeffding components are at most the variance term in \(r_n^*\), uniformly on every compact \(K\subset(0,\infty)^3\) whenever \(P_n=1\). Determine the smallest such order and exhibit a derived nonempty open set \(U\subset(0,\infty)^3\setminus\mathcal R_{\mathrm{bank}}\) with \(U\cap(\{\beta>\alpha\}\cup\{\alpha>1\})\neq\varnothing\) on which the construction works. The scheme must remain total under empty cells and singular empirical local Grams and must not estimate \(f_P\).
body.justification: The correction order and enlarged asymmetric smoothness frontier are the genuinely open mathematical content of the sparse-local branch.
body.gap: The banked first-difference identity works only on \(0<\beta<\alpha\leq1\); Dobriban et al. remove polynomial trends for homoskedastic variance, not the two unequally smooth causal nuisances in a local \(R\)-ratio.
body.consumer: A solution gives an implementable density-free estimator for sparse local windows, including a region with reversed nuisance ordering or propensity smoothness above one.

obligation.what_is_open: A total random-design close-pair or close-tuple construction with specified resolutions and weights, a proof of its product bias and Hoeffding bounds, a minimality argument for its order, and the resulting validity region and strict open extension set.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen handle does not define the admissible class of correction programs, so a smallest order is not yet a well-defined optimization object. More substantively, exact finite-difference cancellation uses geometric stencils that an i.i.d. sample does not supply; replacing them by close random tuples under an arbitrarily nonsmooth density creates normalization and geometric-approximation terms that are not controlled by the listed assumptions without an explicit construction.
obligation.attempted: I formed the natural order-\(r\) binomial finite difference with \(r=\lceil\max\{\alpha,\beta\}\rceil\), which gives the desired deterministic H\"older product order on an exact stencil. I then checked that this algebra alone supplies neither random-tuple availability nor the required Hoeffding variance and hence cannot certify an open extension region.
obligation.partial_result:
There is a finite algebraic Taylor-cancellation candidate.  Put \(r=\lceil\max\{\alpha,\beta\}\rceil\).  For an exact arithmetic stencil and the forward-difference operator
\[
 \Delta_t^r g(x)=\sum_{j=0}^r(-1)^{r-j}{r\choose j}g(x+jt),
\]
the H\"older conditions imply \(|\Delta_t^r\pi_P(x)|\le C|t|^\alpha\) and \(|\Delta_t^r\mu_{0,P}(x)|\le C|t|^\beta\), hence
\[
 |\Delta_t^r\pi_P(x)\,\Delta_t^r\mu_{0,P}(x)|
 \le C|t|^{\alpha+\beta}.
\]
This uses \(r+1\) geometric sites and supplies explicit signed binomial weights.  It does not yet answer the OEQ: random observations do not form exact arithmetic stencils, and under a merely bounded, nonsmooth design density the approximation, normalization, collision terms, and Hoeffding variances of a total close-tuple implementation still require proof.  Nor does this candidate establish minimality among the undefined class of admissible multiresolution programs.
